Wandering through villages, towns, and royal cities, we will surely find some teacher who can teach the doctrine of deliverance.” From then on, wherever they heard it said that wise ascetics and brahmins were present, they went to those places and held discussions. Others were not able to answer the questions asked by them, but they could answer their questions. Thus, having investigated all of Jambudīpa and returned, they came back to their own place and made an agreement: “Friend Kolita, whoever among us first attains the Deathless should inform the other.”

Evaṃ tesu katikaṃ katvā viharantesu satthā vuttānukkamena rājagahaṃ patvā veḷuvanaṃ paṭiggahetvā veḷuvane viharati. Tadā “caratha, bhikkhave, cārikaṃ [M 1.0058] bahujanahitāyā”ti ratanattayaguṇapakāsanatthaṃ uyyojitānaṃ ekasaṭṭhiyā arahantānaṃ antare pañcavaggiyānaṃ abbhantaro assajitthero paṭinivattitvā rājagahaṃ āgato, punadivase pātova pattacīvaramādāya rājagahaṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi. Tasmiṃ samaye upatissaparibbājakopi pātova bhattakiccaṃ katvā paribbājakārāmaṃ gacchanto theraṃ disvā cintesi – “mayā evarūpo pabbajito nāma na diṭṭhapubboyeva, ye loke arahanto vā arahattamaggaṃ vā samāpannā, ayaṃ tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ aññataro, yaṃnūnāhaṃ imaṃ bhikkhuṃ upasaṅkamitvā puccheyyaṃ – ‘kaṃsi tvaṃ, āvuso, uddissa pabbajito, ko vā te satthā, kassa vā tvaṃ dhammaṃ rocesī’”ti? Athassa etadahosi – “akālo kho imaṃ bhikkhuṃ pañhaṃ pucchituṃ, antaragharaṃ paviṭṭho piṇḍāya carati, yaṃnūnāhaṃ imaṃ [V 1.0054] bhikkhuṃ piṭṭhito piṭṭhito anubandheyyaṃ, atthikehi upaññātaṃ magga”nti. So theraṃ laddhapiṇḍapātaṃ aññataraṃ okāsaṃ gacchantaṃ disvā nisīditukāmatañcassa ñatvā attano [P 1.0092] paribbājakapīṭhakaṃ paññāpetvā adāsi, so bhattakiccapariyosānepissa attano kuṇḍikāya udakaṃ adāsi.

Thus, while they were dwelling having made this agreement, the Teacher, in the sequence already mentioned, arrived at Rājagaha, accepted the Veḷuvana, and dwelt there. At that time, among the sixty-one Arahants who had been sent forth to proclaim the virtues of the Triple Gem with the words, “Go forth, O monks, on tour for the welfare of the many,” the Elder Assaji, one of the group of five, turned back and came to Rājagaha. The next day, taking his bowl and robe early in the morning, he entered Rājagaha for alms-food. At that time, the wanderer Upatissa, having finished his meal early in the morning and while going to the wanderers’ park, saw the Elder and thought: “Never before have I seen such a one who has gone forth. Of those in the world who are Arahants or have attained the path to Arahantship, this monk is one of them. What if I were to approach this monk and ask: ‘Friend, on account of whom have you gone forth? Who is your Teacher? And whose Dhamma do you favor?’” Then this thought occurred to him: “It is not the right time to ask this monk a question. He has entered among the houses and is going for alms-food. What if I were to follow this monk from behind? The way is known by those who have need of it.” Seeing the Elder, who had received alms-food, going to a certain place, and knowing his desire to sit down, he spread out his own wanderer’s seat and offered it. At the conclusion of the Elder's meal, he also gave him water from his own water pot.

Evaṃ ācariyavattaṃ katvā katabhattakiccena therena saddhiṃ madhurapaṭisanthāraṃ katvā evamāha – “vippasannāni kho pana te, āvuso, indriyāni, parisuddho chavivaṇṇo pariyodāto, kaṃsi tvaṃ, āvuso, uddissa pabbajito, ko vā te satthā, kassa vā tvaṃ dhammaṃ rocesī”ti pucchi. Thero cintesi – “ime paribbājakā nāma sāsanassa paṭipakkhabhūtā, imassa sāsanassa gambhīrataṃ dassessāmī”ti. Attano navakabhāvaṃ dassento āha – “ahaṃ kho, āvuso, navo acirapabbajito, adhunāgato imaṃ dhammavinayaṃ, na tāvāhaṃ sakkhissāmi vitthārena dhammaṃ desetu”nti. Paribbājako – “ahaṃ upatisso nāma, tvaṃ yathāsattiyā appaṃ vā bahuṃ vā vada, etaṃ nayasatena nayasahassena paṭivijjhituṃ mayhaṃ bhāro”ti cintetvā āha –

Thus, having performed the duties towards a teacher, and having exchanged pleasant and courteous greetings with the Elder who had finished his meal, he said thus: “Friend, your faculties are indeed serene, your skin-complexion is pure and radiant. Friend, on account of whom have you gone forth? Who is your Teacher? And whose Dhamma do you favor?” he asked. The Elder thought: “These wanderers are opponents of the Dispensation. I will show him the profundity of this Dispensation.” Then, indicating his own newness, he said: “Friend, I am a novice, not long gone forth, newly come to this Dhamma and Vinaya. I will not be able to teach the Dhamma in detail.” The wanderer thought: “I am Upatissa by name. Whether you speak little or much according to your ability, to penetrate it with a hundred or a thousand methods is my responsibility,” and said:

“Appaṃ vā bahuṃ vā bhāsassu, atthaṃyeva me brūhi;

Attheneva me attho, kiṃ kāhasi byañjanaṃ bahu”nti. (mahāva. 60);

“Speak little or much, but tell me only the meaning; I have need only of the meaning. What use have I for much phrasing?”

Evaṃ [M 1.0059] vutte thero – “ye dhammā hetuppabhavā”ti (mahāva. 60; apa. thera 1.1.286) gāthamāha. Paribbājako paṭhamapadadvayameva sutvā sahassanayapaṭimaṇḍite sotāpattiphale patiṭṭhahi, itaraṃ padadvayaṃ [P 1.0093] sotāpannakāle niṭṭhāpesi. So sotāpanno hutvā uparivisese appavattante “bhavissati ettha kāraṇa”nti sallakkhetvā theraṃ āha – “bhante, mā upari dhammadesanaṃ vaḍḍhayittha, ettakameva hotu, kuhiṃ amhākaṃ satthā vasatī”ti? “Veḷuvane, āvuso”ti. “Tena hi, bhante, tumhe purato yātha, mayhaṃ eko sahāyako atthi, amhehi ca aññamaññaṃ katikā katā ‘amhesu yo amataṃ paṭhamaṃ adhigacchati, so itarassa ārocetū’ti. Ahaṃ taṃ paṭiññaṃ mocetvā sahāyakaṃ gahetvā tumhākaṃ gatamaggeneva satthu santikaṃ āgamissāmīti pañcapatiṭṭhitena therassa pādesu nipatitvā tikkhattuṃ padakkhiṇaṃ katvā theraṃ uyyojetvā paribbājakārāmābhimukho agamāsi”.

When this was said, the Elder recited the verse: “Whatever phenomena arise from a cause…” The wanderer, having heard only the first two lines, was established in the fruit of stream-entry, which is adorned with a thousand methods. He completed the other two lines at the time of becoming a stream-enterer. Having become a stream-enterer, and when no higher special attainment arose, he considered, “There must be a reason for this,” and said to the Elder: “Venerable sir, do not extend the Dhamma teaching further; let this much be enough. Where does our Teacher dwell?” “In the Veḷuvana, friend.” “Then, venerable sir, you go on ahead. I have a companion, and we have made an agreement with each other: ‘Whoever among us first attains the Deathless should inform the other.’ I, having fulfilled that promise and taking my companion, will come to the Teacher’s presence by the very path you have come.” Then, prostrating at the Elder’s feet with the five-point prostration, circumambulating him three times to the right, and sending the Elder off, he went towards the wanderers’ park.

Atha kho kolitaparibbājako taṃ dūratova āgacchantaṃ disvā, “ajja mayhaṃ sahāyakassa [V 1.0055] mukhavaṇṇo na aññadivasesu viya, addhā tena amataṃ adhigataṃ bhavissatī”ti amatādhigamaṃ pucchi. Sopissa “āmāvuso, amataṃ adhigata”nti paṭijānitvā tameva gāthaṃ abhāsi. Gāthāpariyosāne kolito sotāpattiphale patiṭṭhahitvā āha – “kuhiṃ kira, samma, amhākaṃ satthā vasatī”ti? “Veḷuvane kira, samma, evaṃ no ācariyena assajittherena kathita”nti. “Tena hi, samma, āyāma, satthāraṃ passissāmā”ti. Sāriputtatthero ca nāmesa sadāpi ācariyapūjakova, tasmā sahāyaṃ evamāha – “samma, amhehi adhigataṃ amataṃ amhākaṃ ācariyassa sañcayaparibbājakassāpi kathessāma, bujjhamāno [P 1.0094] paṭivijjhissati, appaṭivijjhanto amhākaṃ saddahitvā satthu, santikaṃ gamissati, buddhānaṃ desanaṃ sutvā maggaphalapaṭivedhaṃ karissatī”ti. Tato dvepi janā sañcayassa santikaṃ agamaṃsu.

Then the wanderer Kolita, seeing him coming from afar, thought: “Today my companion’s facial complexion is not like on other days; surely the Deathless must have been attained by him.” He asked about the attainment of the Deathless. Upatissa, acknowledging to him, “Yes, friend, the Deathless has been attained,” recited that very verse. At the end of the verse, Kolita too was established in the fruit of stream-entry and said: “Dear friend, where, it is said, does our Teacher dwell?” “Dear friend, it is said he dwells in the Veḷuvana; thus it was told by our teacher, the Elder Assaji.” “Then, dear friend, let us go; we shall see the Teacher.” Now, the one named the Elder Sāriputta was always one who honored his teacher; therefore, he said to his companion thus: “Dear friend, the Deathless that has been attained by us, we should also tell our teacher, the wanderer Sañcaya. If he is one who can understand, he will penetrate it. If he is not one who can penetrate it, having faith in us, he will go to the Teacher’s presence, and having heard the teaching of the Buddhas, he will realize the path and fruit.” Then both of them went to the presence of Sañcaya.

Sañcayo te disvāva – “kiṃ, tātā, koci vo amatamaggadesako laddho”ti pucchi. “Āma, ācariya, laddho, buddho loke uppanno, dhammo loke uppanno, saṅgho loke uppanno, tumhe tucche asāre vicaratha, tasmā etha, satthu santikaṃ gamissāmā”ti. “Gacchatha tumhe, nāhaṃ sakkhissāmī”ti[M 1.0060]. “Kiṃ kāraṇāhi”? “Ahaṃ mahājanassa ācariyo hutvā vicariṃ, vicarantassa me antevāsikavāso cāṭiyā udañcanabhāvappatti viya hoti, na sakkhissāmahaṃ antevāsikavāsaṃ vasitu”nti. “Mā evaṃ karittha, ācariyā”ti. “Hotu, tātā, gacchatha tumhe, nāhaṃ sakkhissāmī”ti. Ācariya, loke buddhassa uppannakālato paṭṭhāya mahājano gandhamālādihattho gantvā tameva pūjessati, mayampi tattheva gamissāma. “Tumhe kiṃ karissathā”ti? “Tātā, kiṃ nu kho imasmiṃ loke dandhā bahū, udāhu paṇḍitā”ti. “Dandhā, ācariya, bahū, paṇḍitā ca nāma katipayā eva hontī”ti. “Tena hi, tātā, paṇḍitā paṇḍitassa samaṇassa gotamassa santikaṃ gamissanti, dandhā dandhassa mama santikaṃ āgamissanti[P 1.0095], gacchatha tumhe, nāhaṃ gamissāmī”ti. Te “paññāyissatha tumhe, ācariyā”ti pakkamiṃsu. Tesu gacchantesu sañcayassa parisā bhijji, tasmiṃ khaṇe ārāmo tuccho ahosi. So tucchaṃ ārāmaṃ disvā uṇhaṃ lohitaṃ chaḍḍesi. Tehipi saddhiṃ gacchantesu pañcasu paribbājakasatesu sañcayassa aḍḍhateyyasatāni nivattiṃsu, atha kho te attano antevāsikehi aḍḍhateyyehi paribbājakasatehi saddhiṃ veḷuvanaṃ agamaṃsu.

Sañcaya, seeing them, asked, “My dears, have you found someone who teaches the path to the Deathless?” “Yes, teacher, one has been found. A Buddha has arisen in the world, the Dhamma has arisen in the world, the Saṅgha has arisen in the world. You are practicing in a vain, essenceless way. Therefore, come, let us go to the Teacher's presence.” “You go, I will not be able.” “For what reason?” “I have lived as a teacher of a great multitude. For me, who has lived thus, to live as a resident pupil would be like a large water jar becoming a small water ladle. I will not be able to live the life of a resident pupil.” “Do not act so, teacher.” “Let it be, my dears. You go, I will not be able.” “Teacher, from the time of the Buddha's arising in the world, the great populace, with perfumes and garlands in hand, will go and pay homage only to him. We too will go there. What will you do?” “My dears, in this world, are the dull-witted many, or are the wise many?” “Teacher, the dull-witted are many, and the wise are indeed few.” “Well then, my dears, the wise will go to the presence of the wise ascetic Gotama, while the dull-witted will come to the presence of me, the dull-witted one. You go, I will not go.” They, saying, “You will come to realize this, teacher,” departed. As they were going, Sañcaya's assembly was broken. At that moment, the monastery became empty. Seeing the empty monastery, he vomited hot blood. Among the five hundred wanderers going with them, two hundred and fifty returned to Sañcaya. Then they, together with their own two hundred and fifty wanderer-disciples, went to the Bamboo Grove.

Satthā catuparisamajjhe nisinno dhammaṃ desento te dūratova disvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “ete, bhikkhave, dve sahāyakā āgacchanti kolito ca upatisso ca, etaṃ me sāvakayugaṃ bhavissati aggaṃ bhaddayuga”nti. Te satthāraṃ vanditvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu, nisīditvā ca pana [V 1.0056] bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “labheyyāma mayaṃ, bhante, bhagavato santike pabbajjaṃ, labheyyāma upasampada”nti. “Etha, bhikkhavo”ti bhagavā avoca – “svākkhāto dhammo, caratha brahmacariyaṃ sammā dukkhassa antakiriyāyā”ti. Sabbepi iddhimayapattacīvaradharā saṭṭhivassikattherā viya ahesuṃ.

The Teacher, seated in the midst of the fourfold assembly and teaching the Dhamma, saw them coming from afar and addressed the monks: “Monks, these two companions are coming, Kolita and Upatissa. This will be my pair of disciples, the chief, excellent pair.” They paid homage to the Teacher and sat down to one side. Having sat down, they said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable Sir, may we receive the going forth in the presence of the Blessed One; may we receive the higher ordination.” “Come, monks,” said the Blessed One. “The Dhamma is well-proclaimed. Practice the holy life for the complete ending of suffering.” Immediately after these words, they all became like elders of sixty years’ standing, bearing bowls and robes created by psychic power.

Atha nesaṃ parisāya caritavasena satthā dhammadesanaṃ vaḍḍhesi. Ṭhapetvā dve aggasāvake avasesā arahattaṃ pāpuṇiṃsu, aggasāvakānaṃ pana uparimaggattayakiccaṃ na niṭṭhāsi. Kiṃ kāraṇā? Sāvakapāramiñāṇassa mahantatāya. Athāyasmā mahāmoggallāno pabbajitadivasato [M 1.0061][P 1.0096] sattame divase magadharaṭṭhe kallavālagāmakaṃ upanissāya viharanto thinamiddhe okkamante satthārā saṃvejito thinamiddhaṃ vinodetvā tathāgatena dinnaṃ dhātukammaṭṭhānaṃ suṇantova uparimaggattayakiccaṃ niṭṭhāpetvā sāvakapāramiñāṇassa matthakaṃ patto. Sāriputtattheropi pabbajitadivasato aḍḍhamāsaṃ atikkamitvā satthārā saddhiṃ tameva rājagahaṃ upanissāya sūkarakhataleṇe viharanto attano bhāgineyyassa dīghanakhaparibbājakassa vedanāpariggahasuttante desiyamāne suttānusārena ñāṇaṃ pesetvā parassa vaḍḍhitabhattaṃ paribhuñjanto viya sāvakapāramiñāṇassa matthakaṃ patto. Nanu cāyasmā mahāpañño, atha kasmā mahāmoggallānato ciratarena sāvakapāramiñāṇaṃ pāpuṇīti? Parikammamahantatāya. Yathā hi duggatamanussā yattha katthaci gantukāmā khippameva nikkhamanti, rājūnaṃ pana hatthivāhanakappanādiṃ mahantaṃ parikammaṃ laddhuṃ vaṭṭati, evaṃsampadamidaṃ veditabbaṃ.

Then, according to the disposition of their assembly, the Teacher expanded upon the Dhamma discourse. Setting aside the two chief disciples, the rest of the assembly attained Arahantship. For the chief disciples, however, the task of the three higher paths was not completed. For what reason? Because of the greatness of the knowledge of a disciple’s perfections. Then, on the seventh day from his ordination, the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna, while dwelling near the village of Kallavāḷa in the country of Magadha, was overcome by sloth and torpor. Being roused by the Teacher, he dispelled that sloth and torpor, and while listening to the meditation subject on the elements given by the Tathāgata, he completed the task of the three higher paths and reached the pinnacle of the knowledge of a disciple’s perfections. The Elder Sāriputta, too, half a month having passed since his ordination, while dwelling with the Teacher near that same Rājagaha in the Sūkarakhata cave, as the Vedanāpariggaha Sutta was being taught to his nephew, the wanderer Dīghanakha, sent forth his knowledge in accordance with the sutta and, like one partaking of a meal served by another, reached the pinnacle of the knowledge of a disciple’s perfections. Is not the Venerable Sāriputta of great wisdom? Then why did he attain the knowledge of a disciple’s perfections so much later than Mahāmoggallāna? Because of the greatness of the preliminary work. For just as poor people, wishing to go somewhere, set out quickly, whereas for kings, it is proper to undertake great preparations such as equipping elephant-vehicles and so forth, so should this analogy be understood.

Taṃ divasaññeva pana satthā vaḍḍhamānakacchāyāya veḷuvane sāvakasannipātaṃ katvā dvinnaṃ therānaṃ aggasāvakaṭṭhānaṃ datvā pātimokkhaṃ uddisi. Bhikkhū ujjhāyiṃsu – “satthā mukholokanena bhikkhaṃ deti, aggasāvakaṭṭhānaṃ dadantena nāma paṭhamaṃ pabbajitānaṃ pañcavaggiyānaṃ dātuṃ vaṭṭati, ete anolokentena yasatherappamukhānaṃ pañcapaṇṇāsabhikkhūnaṃ dātuṃ vaṭṭati, ete anolokentena bhaddavaggiyānaṃ [P 1.0097] tiṃsajanānaṃ, ete anolokentena uruvelakassapādīnaṃ tebhātikānaṃ, ete pana ettake mahāthere pahāya sabbapacchā pabbajitānaṃ aggasāvakaṭṭhānaṃ dadantena mukhaṃ oloketvā dinna”nti. Satthā, “kiṃ kathetha, bhikkhave”ti pucchitvā, “idaṃ nāmā”ti vutte “nāhaṃ, bhikkhave, mukhaṃ oloketvā bhikkhaṃ demi, etesaṃ pana attanā attanā patthitapatthitameva demi. Aññātakoṇḍañño hi ekasmiṃ sasse nava vāre aggasassadānaṃ dadanto aggasāvakaṭṭhānaṃ patthetvā nādāsi, aggadhammaṃ pana arahattaṃ sabbapaṭhamaṃ paṭivijjhituṃ patthetvā adāsī”ti. “Kadā pana bhagavā”ti? “Suṇissatha, bhikkhave”ti. “Āma, bhante”ti, bhagavā atītaṃ āhari –

On that very day, the Teacher, while dwelling in the Veḷuvana monastery, convened an assembly of disciples, and after giving the position of chief disciples to the two elders, he recited the Pātimokkha. The monks complained, saying: “The Teacher gives favors by showing partiality. When giving the position of chief disciples, it would have been proper to give it first to the group of five who went forth. If not considering them, it would have been proper to give it to the fifty-five monks headed by the Elder Yasa. If not considering them, to the thirty men of the Bhaddavaggiya group. If not considering them, to the three Kassapa brothers of Uruvelā. But having disregarded so many great elders, in giving the position of chief disciples to those who went forth last of all, he has given it with partiality.” The Teacher asked, “Monks, what are you discussing?” and upon being told, “It is this matter,” he said: “Monks, I do not give favors by showing partiality. Rather, I give to them only what each has respectively aspired for. Indeed, Aññāta Koṇḍañña, when giving the first-fruit offering of the harvest nine times from a single crop, did not give it aspiring for the position of chief disciple; rather, he gave it aspiring to be the very first to penetrate the supreme Dhamma, Arahantship.” When they asked, “But when, Blessed One?” he said, “Listen, monks.” When they replied, “Yes, venerable sir,” the Blessed One related a story from the past:

Bhikkhave[V 1.0057], ito ekanavutikappe vipassī nāma bhagavā loke udapādi. Tadā mahākāḷo cūḷakāḷoti dvebhātikā kuṭumbikā mahantaṃ sālikkhettaṃ [M 1.0062] vapāpesuṃ. Athekadivasaṃ cūḷakāḷo sālikkhettaṃ gantvā ekaṃ sāligabbhaṃ phāletvā khādi, taṃ atimadhuraṃ ahosi. So buddhappamukhassa saṅghassa sāligabbhadānaṃ dātukāmo hutvā jeṭṭhabhātikaṃ upasaṅkamitvā, “bhātika, sāligabbhaṃ phāletvā buddhānaṃ anucchavikaṃ katvā pacāpetvā dānaṃ demā”ti āha. “Kiṃ vadesi, tāta, sāligabbhaṃ phāletvā dānaṃ nāma neva atīte bhūtapubbaṃ, na anāgatepi bhavissati, mā sassaṃ nāsayī”ti; vuttopi so punappunaṃ yāciyeva[P 1.0098]. Atha naṃ bhātā, “tena hi sālikkhettaṃ dve koṭṭhāse katvā mama koṭṭhāsaṃ anāmasitvā attano koṭṭhāse khette yaṃ icchasi, taṃ karohī”ti āha. So “sādhū”ti khettaṃ vibhajitvā bahū manusse hatthakammaṃ yācitvā sāligabbhaṃ phāletvā nirudakena khīrena pacāpetvā sappimadhusakkharādīhi yojetvā buddhappamukhassa bhikkhusaṅghassa dānaṃ datvā bhattakiccapariyosāne – “idaṃ, bhante, mama aggadānaṃ aggadhammassa sabbapaṭhamaṃ paṭivedhāya saṃvattatū”ti āha. Satthā “evaṃ hotū”ti anumodanamakāsi.

“Monks, ninety-one aeons from the present, the Blessed One named Vipassī arose in the world. At that time, two householder brothers, Mahākāḷa and Cūḷakāḷa, had a large rice field sown. Then one day, Cūḷakāḷa went to the rice field, broke open a young grain of rice and ate it, and it was exceedingly sweet. Desiring to give an offering of young rice grain to the Saṅgha headed by the Buddha, he approached his elder brother and said, ‘Brother, let us break open the young rice grain, have it cooked in a manner suitable for the Buddhas, and give it as an offering.’ ‘What are you saying, dear brother? An offering made by breaking open young rice grain has never happened in the past, nor will it happen in the future. Do not destroy the crop.’ Though spoken to thus, he pleaded again and again. Then his brother said to him, ‘In that case, divide the rice field into two portions, and without touching my portion, do whatever you wish in your portion of the field.’ He said, ‘Very well,’ and having divided the field, he requested manual labor from many people, broke open the young rice grain, had it cooked with pure milk, and mixed it with ghee, honey, sugar, and so forth. He then gave the offering to the community of monks headed by the Buddha. At the conclusion of the meal, he said: ‘Venerable sir, may this first-fruit offering of mine lead to my penetrating the supreme Dhamma first among all.’ The Teacher gave his approval, saying, ‘So be it.’”

So khettaṃ gantvā olokento sakalakkhettaṃ kaṇṇikabaddhehi viya sālisīsehi sañchannaṃ disvā pañcavidhapītiṃ paṭilabhitvā, “lābhā vata me”ti cintetvā puthukakāle puthukaggaṃ nāma adāsi, gāmavāsīhi saddhiṃ aggasassadānaṃ nāma adāsi, lāyane lāyanaggaṃ, veṇikaraṇe veṇaggaṃ, kalāpādīsu kalāpaggaṃ, khalaggaṃ, khalabhaṇḍaggaṃ, koṭṭhagganti. Evaṃ ekasasse nava vāre aggadānaṃ adāsi. Tassa sabbavāresu gahitagahitaṭṭhānaṃ paripūri, sassaṃ atirekaṃ uṭṭhānasampannaṃ ahosi. Dhammo hi nāmesa attānaṃ rakkhantaṃ rakkhati. Tenāha bhagavā –

He went to the field and, looking on, saw the entire field covered with heads of rice as if adorned with rosettes. Experiencing the five kinds of joy, he thought, ‘Ah, what a gain for me!’ At the time of making flattened rice, he gave the first offering of flattened rice; with the villagers, he gave the first offering of the harvest; at the time of reaping, the first offering of reaping; when binding handfuls, the first offering of handfuls; when making sheaves, the first offering of sheaves; the first offering of the threshing floor; the first offering of threshing; the first offering of measuring; and the first offering of the granary. In this way, from a single crop, he gave a first-fruit offering nine times. On all these occasions, whatever was taken was replenished, and the crop was exceedingly abundant and successful. For indeed, the Dhamma protects one who lives in accordance with the Dhamma. Therefore, the Blessed One said:

“Dhammo [P 1.0099] have rakkhati dhammacāriṃ,

Dhammo suciṇṇo sukhamāvahāti;

Esānisaṃso dhamme suciṇṇe,

Na duggatiṃ gacchati dhammacārī”ti. (theragā. 303; jā. 1.10.102) –

“The Dhamma surely protects one who lives by the Dhamma; the Dhamma, well-practiced, brings happiness. This is the benefit of the Dhamma being well-practiced: one who lives by the Dhamma does not go to a woeful state.”

“Evamesa [M 1.0063] vipassīsammāsambuddhakāle aggadhammaṃ paṭhamaṃ paṭivijjhituṃ patthento nava vāre aggadānāni adāsi. Ito satasahassakappamatthake pana haṃsavatīnagare padumuttarasambuddhakālepi sattāhaṃ mahādānaṃ datvā tassa bhagavato pādamūle nipajjitvā aggadhammassa paṭhamaṃ paṭivijjhanatthameva [V 1.0058] patthanaṃ ṭhapesi. Iti iminā patthitameva mayā dinnaṃ, nāhaṃ, bhikkhave, mukhaṃ oloketvā demī”ti.

“Thus, in the time of the Perfectly Enlightened One Vipassī, this one, aspiring to be the first to penetrate the supreme Dhamma, gave first-fruit offerings nine times. Furthermore, one hundred thousand aeons ago from the present, in the city of Haṃsavatī, during the time of the Perfectly Enlightened One Padumuttara, after giving a great offering for seven days, he lay down at the feet of that Blessed One and made the aspiration solely for the sake of being the first to penetrate the supreme Dhamma. Therefore, what was aspired for by him has been given by me. Monks, I do not give by showing partiality.”

“Yasakulaputtappamukhā pañcapaññāsa janā kiṃ kammaṃ kariṃsu, bhante”ti? “Etepi ekassa buddhassa santike arahattaṃ patthentā bahuṃ puññakammaṃ katvā aparabhāge anuppanne buddhe sahāyakā hutvā vaggabandhanena puññāni karontā anāthamatasarīrāni paṭijaggantā vicariṃsu. Te ekadivasaṃ sagabbhaṃ itthiṃ kālakataṃ disvā, ‘jhāpessāmā’ti susānaṃ hariṃsu. Tesu pañca jane ‘tumhe jhāpethā’ti susāne ṭhapetvā sesā gāmaṃ paviṭṭhā. Yasadārako taṃ matasarīraṃ sūlehi vijjhitvā parivattetvā parivattetvā jhāpento asubhasaññaṃ paṭilabhi, itaresampi catunnaṃ janānaṃ – ‘passatha, bho, imaṃ sarīraṃ tattha tattha viddhaṃsitacammaṃ, kabaragorūpaṃ viya asuciṃ duggandhaṃ paṭikūla’nti [P 1.0100] dassesi. Tepi tattha asubhasaññaṃ paṭilabhiṃsu. Te pañcapi janā gāmaṃ gantvā sesasahāyakānaṃ kathayiṃsu. Yaso pana dārako gehaṃ gantvā mātāpitūnañca bhariyāya ca kathesi. Te sabbepi asubhaṃ bhāvayiṃsu. Idametesaṃ pubbakammaṃ. Teneva yasassa itthāgāre susānasaññā uppajji, tāya ca upanissayasampattiyā sabbesampi visesādhigamo nibbatti. Evaṃ imepi attanā patthitameva labhiṃsu. Nāhaṃ mukhaṃ oloketvā dammī”ti.

“Venerable sir, what deed did the fifty-five people headed by the noble son Yasa perform?” “These too, aspiring for Arahantship in the presence of one Buddha, performed much meritorious action. Later, when no Buddha had arisen, they became companions and, forming a group, performed meritorious deeds while tending to the bodies of the unsupported deceased. One day, seeing a pregnant woman who had died, they carried her to the charnel ground, thinking, ‘We will cremate her.’ Leaving five people there with the instruction, ‘You cremate her,’ the rest entered the village. The young man Yasa, while cremating that dead body by piercing it with stakes and turning it over and over, gained the perception of repulsiveness. He then pointed it out to the other four people, saying, ‘See, friends, this body—its skin is destroyed here and there, like a mottled ox, impure, foul-smelling, and repulsive.’ They too gained the perception of repulsiveness there. All five people, going to the village, told their remaining companions. The young man Yasa, however, went home and also related it to his parents and wife. They all then developed meditation on repulsiveness. This was their past kamma. Because of that, the perception of a charnel ground arose for Yasa in the women's quarters, and through the accomplishment of that supporting condition, the attainment of distinction was accomplished for all of them. Thus, these too attained what they themselves had aspired for. I do not give by looking at faces.”

“Bhaddavaggiyasahāyakā pana kiṃ kammaṃ kariṃsu, bhante”ti? “Etepi pubbabuddhānaṃ santike arahattaṃ patthetvā puññāni katvā aparabhāge anuppanne buddhe tiṃsa dhuttā hutvā tuṇḍilovādaṃ sutvā saṭṭhivassasahassāni pañca sīlāni rakkhiṃsu. Evaṃ imepi attanā patthitameva labhiṃsu. Nāhaṃ mukhaṃ oloketvā dammī”ti.

“Venerable sir, what deed did the Bhaddavaggiya companions perform?” “These too, aspiring for Arahantship in the presence of past Buddhas, performed meritorious deeds. In a later period, when no Buddha had arisen, thirty of them became profligates. Upon hearing the advice of Tuṇḍila, they observed the five precepts for sixty thousand years. Thus, they too attained just what they had aspired for. I do not give by looking at faces.”

“Uruvelakassapādayo pana kiṃ kammaṃ kariṃsu, bhante”ti? “Tepi arahattameva patthetvā puññāni kariṃsu. Ito hi dvenavutikappe tisso [M 1.0064] phussoti dve buddhā uppajjiṃsu. Phussabuddhassa mahindo nāma rājā pitā ahosi. Tasmiṃ pana sambodhiṃ patte rañño kaniṭṭhaputto paṭhamaaggasāvako purohitaputto dutiyaaggasāvako ahosi. Rājā satthu santikaṃ gantvā – ‘jeṭṭhaputto me buddho, kaniṭṭhaputto paṭhamaaggasāvako, purohitaputto dutiyaaggasāvako’ti te oloketvā, ‘mameva buddho, mameva dhammo, mameva saṅgho, namo tassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassā’ti tikkhattuṃ udānaṃ udānetvā satthu pādamūle nipajjitvā[P 1.0101], ‘bhante, idāni me navutivassasahassaparimāṇassa āyuno koṭiyaṃ nisīditvā niddāyanakālo viya aññesaṃ gehadvāraṃ agantvā yāvāhaṃ jīvāmi, tāva me cattāro paccaye adhivāsethā’ti [V 1.0059] paṭiññaṃ gahetvā nibaddhaṃ buddhupaṭṭhānaṃ karoti. Rañño pana aparepi tato puttā ahesuṃ. Tesu jeṭṭhassa pañca yodhasatāni parivārāni, majjhimassa tīṇi, kaniṭṭhassa dve. Te ‘mayampi bhātikaṃ bhojessāmā’ti pitaraṃ okāsaṃ yācitvā alabhamānā punappunaṃ yācantāpi alabhitvā paccante kupite tassa vūpasamanatthāya pesitā paccantaṃ vūpasametvā pitu santikaṃ āgamiṃsu. Atha ne pitā āliṅgitvā sīse cumbitvā, ‘varaṃ vo, tātā, dammī’ti āha.

“But what deeds did Uruvelā Kassapa and the others perform, venerable sir?” “They too, aspiring for Arahantship itself, performed meritorious deeds. For in the ninety-second aeon from this one, two Buddhas, Tissa and Phussa, arose. The father of Phussa Buddha was a king named Mahinda. When Phussa Buddha attained enlightenment, the king’s younger son became the first chief disciple, and the chaplain’s son became the second chief disciple. The king went to the Teacher and, looking at them, said: ‘My eldest son is the Buddha, my younger son is the first chief disciple, and the chaplain’s son is the second chief disciple!’ Then, uttering the exclamation three times, ‘The Buddha is mine alone, the Dhamma is mine alone, the Saṅgha is mine alone! Homage to that Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One!’, the king prostrated himself at the Teacher's feet and said: ‘Venerable sir, now, having reached the end of my ninety-thousand-year lifespan, it is as if it is time for my repose. For as long as I live, may you not go to the doorways of others but consent to receive the four requisites from me.’ Having taken this promise, he constantly attended upon the Buddha. Now, the king also had three other sons. The eldest had five hundred warriors as his retinue, the middle one had three hundred, and the youngest had two hundred. Thinking, ‘We too shall provide for our brother,’ they asked their father for the opportunity, but not receiving it, they asked again and again without receiving it. When the border region was in revolt, they were sent to pacify it. After pacifying the border, they returned to their father. Then their father embraced them, kissed their heads, and said, ‘I shall give you a boon, my dears.’”

“Te ‘sādhu devā’ti varaṃ gahitakaṃ katvā puna katipāhaccayena pitarā ‘gaṇhatha, tātā, vara’nti vuttā, “deva, amhākaṃ aññena kenaci attho natthi, ito paṭṭhāya mayaṃ bhātikaṃ bhojessāma, imaṃ no varaṃ dehī”ti āhaṃsu. ‘Na demi, tātā’ti. ‘Niccakālaṃ adento satta saṃvaccharāni detha, devā’ti. ‘Na demi, tātā’ti. ‘Tena hi cha pañca cattāri tīṇi dve ekaṃ saṃvaccharaṃ detha, devā’ti. ‘Na demi, tātā’ti. ‘Tena hi, deva, satta māse dethā’ti. ‘Cha māse pañca māse cattāro māse tayo māse detha, devā’ti. ‘Na demi, tātā’ti. ‘Hotu, deva, ekekassa no ekekaṃ māsaṃ katvā tayo māse dethā’ti. ‘Sādhu, tātā, tena hi tayo māse bhojethā’ti āha. Te tuṭṭhā rājānaṃ vanditvā sakaṭṭhānameva gatā. Tesaṃ pana tiṇṇampi ekova koṭṭhāgāriko, ekova āyuttako, tassa dvādasanahutā purisaparivārā. Te te pakkosāpetvā[P 1.0102], ‘mayaṃ imaṃ temāsaṃ dasa sīlāni gahetvā dve kāsāvāni [M 1.0065] nivāsetvā satthārā sahavāsaṃ vasissāma, tumhe ettakaṃ nāma dānavattaṃ gahetvā devasikaṃ navutisahassānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ yodhasahassassa ca sabbaṃ khādanīyabhojanīyaṃ pavatteyyātha. Mayañhi ito paṭṭhāya na kiñci vakkhāmā’ti vadiṃsu.

“They said, ‘Very well, Your Majesty,’ and having accepted the boon in principle, after a few days their father said, ‘Take your boon, my dears.’ They replied, ‘Your Majesty, we have no need for anything else. From now on, we will provide for our brother. Grant us this boon.’ ‘I will not grant it, my dears.’ ‘If you will not grant it permanently, grant it for seven years, Your Majesty.’ ‘I will not grant it, my dears.’ ‘In that case, grant it for six, five, four, three, two, or one year, Your Majesty.’ ‘I will not grant it, my dears.’ ‘In that case, Your Majesty, grant it for seven months.’ ‘Grant it for six months, five months, four months, three months, Your Majesty.’ ‘I will not grant it, my dears.’ ‘So be it, Your Majesty. Grant it for three months, making it one month for each of us.’ ‘Good, my dears. In that case, you may provide for him for three months,’ he said. Pleased, they paid homage to the king and went to their own quarters. Now, all three of them had only one storekeeper and only one commissioner, and he had a retinue of one hundred and twenty thousand men. They had them summoned and said, ‘For these three months, we will undertake the ten precepts, don the two ochre robes, and dwell together with the Teacher. You must undertake this duty of giving and daily provide all the solid and soft food for ninety thousand monks and a thousand warriors. For from now on, we will say nothing at all.’”

“Te tayopi janā parivārasahassaṃ gahetvā dasa sīlāni samādāya kāsāyavatthāni nivāsetvā vihāreyeva vasiṃsu. Koṭṭhāgāriko ca āyuttako ca ekato hutvā tiṇṇaṃ bhātikānaṃ koṭṭhāgārehi vārena vārena dānavattaṃ gahetvā dānaṃ denti, kammakārānaṃ pana puttā yāgubhattādīnaṃ atthāya rodanti. Te tesaṃ bhikkhusaṅghe anāgateyeva yāgubhattādīni denti. Bhikkhusaṅghassa bhattakiccāvasāne kiñci atirekaṃ na bhūtapubbaṃ. Te ‘aparabhāge dārakānaṃ demā’ti attanāpi gahetvā khādiṃsu. Manuññaṃ āhāraṃ disvā adhivāsetuṃ nāsakkhiṃsu. Te pana caturāsītisahassā ahesuṃ. Te saṅghassa dinnadānavattaṃ khāditvā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā pettivisaye nibbattiṃsu. Tebhātikā pana purisasahassena saddhiṃ kālaṃ katvā devaloke nibbattitvā devalokā manussalokaṃ, manussalokā devalokaṃ saṃsarantā dvenavutikappe khepesuṃ. ‘Evaṃ [V 1.0060] te tayo bhātaro arahattaṃ patthentā tadā kalyāṇakammaṃ kariṃsu. Te attanā patthitameva labhiṃsu. Nāhaṃ mukhaṃ oloketvā dammī’”ti.

“Those three persons, taking a retinue of a thousand, undertook the ten precepts, donned saffron-dyed robes, and dwelt right in the monastery. The storekeeper and the commissioner, joining together, took turns taking up the alms-duty from the storerooms of the three brothers and giving alms. But the workers' children cried for rice-gruel and cooked rice. Even before the community of bhikkhus arrived, they gave rice-gruel, cooked rice, and other things to them. At the conclusion of the meal-duty for the community of bhikkhus, nothing extra had ever been left over. Thinking, ‘Later we will give to the children,’ they themselves also took and ate. Seeing the delightful food, they were unable to resist. Now, they were eighty-four thousand in number. Having eaten the alms-offering given to the Saṅgha, after the breaking up of the body, after death, they were reborn in the sphere of petas. The three brothers, however, together with a thousand men, having passed away, were reborn in the deva world. Wandering from the deva world to the human world, and from the human world to the deva world, they passed ninety-two aeons. Thus, those three brothers, aspiring to Arahantship, performed that meritorious deed at that time. They obtained exactly what they themselves had aspired to. I do not give by looking at faces.”

Tadā pana [P 1.0103] tesaṃ āyuttako bimbisāro rājā ahosi, koṭṭhāgāriko visākho upāsako. Tayo rājakumārā tayo jaṭilā ahesuṃ. Tesaṃ kammakārā tadā petesu nibbattitvā sugatiduggativasena saṃsarantā imasmiṃ kappe cattāri buddhantarāni petalokeyeva nibbattiṃsu. Te imasmiṃ kappe sabbapaṭhamaṃ uppannaṃ cattālīsavassasahassāyukaṃ kakusandhaṃ bhagavantaṃ upasaṅkamitvā, “amhākaṃ āhāraṃ labhanakālaṃ ācikkhathā”ti pucchiṃsu. So “mama tāva kāle na labhissatha, mama pacchato mahāpathaviyā yojanamattaṃ abhiruḷhāya koṇāgamano nāma buddho uppajjissati, taṃ puccheyyāthā”ti āha. Te tattakaṃ kālaṃ khepetvā tasmiṃ uppanne taṃ pucchiṃsu. Sopi “mama kāle na labhissatha, mama pacchato mahāpathaviyā yojanamattaṃ abhiruḷhāya kassapo nāma [M 1.0066] buddho uppajjissati, taṃ puccheyyāthā”ti āha. Te tattakaṃ kālaṃ khepetvā tasmiṃ uppanne taṃ pucchiṃsu. Sopi “mama kāle na labhissatha, mama pana pacchato mahāpathaviyā yojanamattaṃ abhiruḷhāya gotamo nāma buddho uppajjissati, tadā tumhākaṃ ñātako bimbisāro nāma rājā bhavissati, so satthu dānaṃ datvā tumhākaṃ pattiṃ pāpessati, tadā labhissathā”ti āha. Tesaṃ ekaṃ buddhantaraṃ svedivasasadisaṃ ahosi. Te tathāgate uppanne bimbisāraraññā paṭhamadivasaṃ dāne dinne pattiṃ alabhitvā rattibhāge bheravasaddaṃ katvā rañño attānaṃ dassayiṃsu. So punadivase veḷuvanaṃ gantvā tathāgatassa [P 1.0104] taṃ pavattiṃ ārocesi.

At that time, their steward was King Bimbisāra, and the storekeeper was the lay follower Visākha. Their workers, at that time, having been reborn among the petas and wandering by way of good and bad destinations, were reborn only in the peta world for four Buddha-intervals in this aeon. In this aeon, they first approached the Blessed One Kakusandha, who had arisen with a lifespan of forty thousand years, and asked, 'Venerable Sir, please tell us the time when we will obtain food.' He replied, 'You will not obtain it in my time. After me, when the great earth has risen by a yojana, a Buddha named Koṇāgamana will arise. You should ask him.' Having passed that much time, when he arose, they asked him. He too said, 'You will not obtain it in my time. After me, when the great earth has risen by a yojana, a Buddha named Kassapa will arise. You should ask him.' Having passed that much time, when he arose, they asked him. He also said, 'You will not obtain it in my time. But after me, when the great earth has risen by a yojana, a Buddha named Gotama will arise. At that time, your kinsman, a king named Bimbisāra, will exist. He will give a gift to the Teacher and cause the share of merit to reach you. Then you will obtain it.' For them, one Buddha-interval was like the next day. When the Tathāgata arose, on the first day when King Bimbisāra had given a gift, not receiving the share of merit, in the night-time they made a terrifying sound and showed themselves to the king. The next day, he went to Veḷuvana and reported that event to the Tathāgata.

Satthā, “mahārāja, ito dvenavutikappamatthake phussabuddhakāle ete tava ñātakā, bhikkhusaṅghassa dinnadānavattaṃ khāditvā petaloke nibbattitvā saṃsarantā kakusandhādayo buddhe pucchitvā tehi idañcidañca vuttā ettakaṃ kālaṃ tava dānaṃ paccāsīsamānā hiyyo tayā dāne dinne pattiṃ alabhamānā evamakaṃsū”ti āha. “Kiṃ pana, bhante, idānipi dinne labhissantī”ti? “Āma, mahārājā”ti. Rājā buddhappamukhaṃ bhikkhusaṅghaṃ nimantetvā punadivase mahādānaṃ datvā, “bhante, ito tesaṃ petānaṃ dibbaannapānaṃ sampajjatū”ti pattiṃ adāsi, tesaṃ tatheva nibbatti. Punadivase naggā hutvā attānaṃ dassesuṃ. Rājā “ajja, bhante, naggā hutvā attānaṃ dassesu”nti ārocesi. “Vatthāni te na dinnāni, mahārājā”ti. Rājāpi punadivase buddhappamukhassa bhikkhusaṅghassa cīvaradānaṃ datvā, “ito tesaṃ petānaṃ dibbavatthāni hontū”ti pāpesi. Taṅkhaṇaññeva tesaṃ dibbavatthāni uppajjiṃsu. Te petattabhāvaṃ [V 1.0061] vijahitvā dibbattabhāve saṇṭhahiṃsu. Satthā anumodanaṃ karonto “tirokuṭṭesu tiṭṭhantī”tiādinā (khu. pā. 7.1; pe. va. 14) tirokuṭṭānumodanaṃ akāsi. Anumodanāvasāne caturāsītiyā pāṇasahassānaṃ dhammābhisamayo ahosi. Iti satthā tebhātikajaṭilānaṃ vatthuṃ kathetvā imampi dhammadesanaṃ āhari.

The Teacher said: 'Great King, ninety-two aeons from this one, in the time of the Buddha Phussa, these kinsmen of yours, having eaten the provisions of the offering given to the community of bhikkhus, were reborn in the peta world. Wandering thus, they asked the Buddhas, Kakusandha and others, and having been told this and that by them, for so long a time they were hoping for your gift. Yesterday, when the gift was given by you, not receiving the share of merit, they acted thus.' 'But, Venerable Sir, if it is given now, will they receive it?' 'Yes, Great King.' The king invited the community of bhikkhus with the Buddha at its head and the next day gave a great offering. He gave the share of merit, saying, 'Venerable Sir, from this, may divine food and drink arise for those petas.' It came to be for them just so. The next day, they showed themselves, being naked. The king reported, 'Venerable Sir, today they showed themselves, being naked.' 'Great King, you have not given them clothes.' The king also, the next day, gave an offering of robes to the community of bhikkhus with the Buddha at its head and dedicated the merit, saying, 'From this, may divine garments come to be for those petas.' At that very moment, divine garments arose for them. They, having abandoned the peta-existence, were established in a divine existence. The Teacher, giving the anumodanā, recited the Tirokuṭṭa Anumodanā beginning with 'tirokuṭṭesu tiṭṭhanti'. At the conclusion of the anumodanā, for eighty-four thousand living beings, there was the comprehension of the Dhamma. Thus, the Teacher, having related the story of the three matted-hair ascetic brothers, also delivered this Dhamma discourse.

Aggasāvakā pana, “bhante, kiṃ kariṃsū”ti? “Aggasāvakabhāvāya patthanaṃ kariṃsu”. Ito kappasatasahassādhikassa hi kappānaṃ asaṅkhyeyyassa matthake sāriputto brāhmaṇamahāsālakule nibbatti, nāmena saradamāṇavo [M 1.0067] nāma ahosi. Moggallāno gahapatimahāsālakule [P 1.0105] nibbatti, nāmena sirivaḍḍhanakuṭumbiko nāma ahosi. Te ubhopi sahapaṃsukīḷakā sahāyakā ahesuṃ. Tesu saradamāṇavo pitu accayena kusalantakaṃ mahādhanaṃ paṭipajjitvā ekadivasaṃ rahogato cintesi – “ahaṃ idhalokattabhāvameva jānāmi, no paralokattabhāvaṃ. Jātasattānañca maraṇaṃ nāma dhuvaṃ, mayā ekaṃ pabbajjaṃ pabbajitvā mokkhadhammagavesanaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭatī”ti. So sahāyakaṃ upasaṅkamitvā āha – “samma sirivaḍḍhana, ahaṃ pabbajitvā mokkhadhammaṃ gavesissāmi, tvaṃ mayā saddhiṃ pabbajituṃ sakkhissasi, na sakkhissasī”ti? “Na sakkhissāmi, samma, tvaṃyeva pabbajāhī”ti. So cintesi – “paralokaṃ gacchanto sahāye vā ñātimitte vā gahetvā gato nāma natthi, attanā kataṃ attanova hotī”ti. Tato ratanakoṭṭhāgāraṃ vivarāpetvā kapaṇaddhikavaṇibbakayācakānaṃ mahādānaṃ datvā pabbatapādaṃ pavisitvā isipabbajjaṃ pabbaji. Tassa eko dve tayoti evaṃ anupabbajjaṃ pabbajitā catusattatisahassamattā jaṭilā ahesuṃ. So pañca abhiññā, aṭṭha ca samāpattiyo nibbattetvā tesaṃ jaṭilānaṃ kasiṇaparikammaṃ ācikkhi. Tepi sabbe pañca abhiññā aṭṭha ca samāpattiyo nibbattesuṃ.

Then, regarding the chief disciples, it was asked, "Venerable Sir, what did they do?" "They made the aspiration for the state of chief discipleship." Indeed, one incalculable aeon and one hundred thousand kappas ago from this present aeon, Sāriputta was born into a great brahmin family of vast wealth, and was named the youth Sarada. Moggallāna was born into a great householder family of vast wealth, and was named the householder Sirivaḍḍhana. The two were childhood playmates and companions. Among them, the youth Sarada, after his father’s passing, inherited a vast family fortune. One day, in seclusion, he reflected: "I know only existence in this world, not existence in the next. Death is certain for beings that are born. It is fitting for me to go forth and seek the state of liberation." He approached his friend and said, "Friend Sirivaḍḍhana, I will go forth and seek the state of liberation. Can you go forth with me, or not?" "I cannot, friend. You go forth alone." He thought, "No one takes friends or relatives when departing to the next world. What one does, belongs to oneself alone." Then he had his treasure-house opened and gave a great donation to the destitute, travelers, and beggars. He entered the foothills of a mountain and went forth into the ascetic life of a seer. Following his example, one, two, three, and so on, went forth after him, until there were seventy-four thousand matted-hair ascetics. He developed the five supernormal knowledges and the eight attainments and taught those matted-hair ascetics the preliminary kasiṇa practice. They too all developed the five supernormal knowledges and the eight attainments.

Tena samayena anomadassī nāma sammāsambuddho loke udapādi. Nagaraṃ candavatī nāma ahosi, pitā yasavā nāma khattiyo, mātā yasodharā nāma devī, bodhi ajjunarukkho, nisabho ca anomo ca dve aggasāvakā, varuṇo nāma upaṭṭhāko, sundarā ca sumanā ca dve aggasāvikā ahesuṃ. Āyu vassasatasahassaṃ ahosi, sarīraṃ aṭṭhapaññāsahatthubbedhaṃ[P 1.0106], sarīrappabhā dvādasayojanaṃ phari, bhikkhusatasahassaparivāro ahosi. So ekadivasaṃ paccūsakāle mahākaruṇāsamāpattito vuṭṭhāya lokaṃ volokento saradatāpasaṃ disvā, “ajja mayhaṃ saradatāpasassaṃ santikaṃ gatapaccayena dhammadesanā ca mahatī bhavissati, so ca aggasāvakaṭṭhānaṃ patthessati, tassa sahāyako sirivaḍḍhanakuṭumbiko dutiyasāvakaṭṭhānaṃ, desanāpariyosāne [V 1.0062] cassa parivārā catusattatisahassamattā jaṭilā arahattaṃ pāpuṇissanti, mayā tattha gantuṃ vaṭṭatī”ti attano pattacīvaramādāya aññaṃ kañci anāmantetvā sīho viya ekacaro hutvā saradatāpasassa [M 1.0068] antevāsikesu phalāphalatthāya gatesu “buddhabhāvaṃ me jānātū”ti adhiṭṭhahitvā passantasseva saradatāpasassa ākāsato otaritvā pathaviyaṃ patiṭṭhāsi. Saradatāpaso buddhānubhāvañceva sarīranipphattiñcassa disvā lakkhaṇamante sammasitvā “imehi lakkhaṇehi samannāgato nāma agāramajjhe vasanto rājā hoti cakkavattī, pabbajanto loke vivaṭṭacchado sabbaññubuddho hoti. Ayaṃ puriso nissaṃsayaṃ buddho”ti jānitvā paccuggamanaṃ katvā pañcapatiṭṭhitena vanditvā aggāsanaṃ paññāpetvā adāsi. Nisīdi bhagavā paññatte aggāsane. Saradatāpasopi attano anucchavikaṃ āsanaṃ gahetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi.

At that time, a Perfectly Self-Enlightened One named Anomadassī arose in the world. The city was named Candavatī, his father was the Khattiya Yasavā, his mother was Queen Yasodharā, his Bodhi tree was the Ajjuna tree, and his two chief disciples were Nisabha and Anoma. His attendant was named Varuṇa, and his two chief female disciples were Sundarā and Sumanā. His lifespan was one hundred thousand years, his body was fifty-eight cubits tall, the radiance of his body spread for twelve yojanas, and he had a retinue of one hundred thousand bhikkhus. One day, at dawn, having emerged from the attainment of great compassion and surveying the world, he saw the ascetic Sarada. He reflected, 'Today, by reason of my going to the ascetic Sarada, there will be a great Dhamma teaching. He will aspire to the position of chief disciple, and his companion, the householder Sirivaḍḍhana, to the position of the second disciple. At the conclusion of the teaching, his retinue of seventy-four thousand matted-hair ascetics will attain Arahantship. It is fitting for me to go there.' Taking his bowl and robe without informing anyone else, he went alone like a lion. While the disciples of the ascetic Sarada had gone to gather fruits, he made a resolution, 'Let him recognize my Buddhahood,' and descending from the sky right before the ascetic Sarada’s eyes, he stood on the ground. The ascetic Sarada, seeing the Buddha’s majestic power and the perfection of his body, reflected on the treatises concerning the marks of a great man and thought, 'A person endowed with these marks, if dwelling in the household life, becomes a wheel-turning monarch. If he goes forth, he becomes a Buddha with the veil removed, an All-Knowing One. Without a doubt, this man is the Buddha.' Understanding this, he went forward to greet him, paid homage with the five-point prostration, prepared the highest seat, and offered it. The Blessed One sat on the prepared highest seat. The ascetic Sarada also took a suitable seat and sat to one side.

Tasmiṃ samaye catusattatisahassajaṭilā paṇītapaṇītāni ojavantāni phalāphalāni gahetvā ācariyassa santikaṃ sampattā buddhānañceva ācariyassa ca nisinnāsanaṃ oloketvā āhaṃsu – “ācariya[P 1.0107], mayaṃ ‘imasmiṃ loke tumhehi mahantataro natthī’ti vicarāma, ayaṃ pana puriso tumhehi mahantataro maññe”ti? “Tātā, kiṃ vadetha, sāsapena saddhiṃ aṭṭhasaṭṭhiyojanasatasahassubbedhaṃ sineruṃ samaṃ kātuṃ icchatha, sabbaññubuddhena saddhiṃ mamaṃ upamaṃ mā karittha puttakā”ti. Atha te tāpasā, “sacāyaṃ ittarasatto abhavissa, amhākaṃ ācariyo na evarūpaṃ upamaṃ āharissa, yāva mahā vatāyaṃ puriso”ti sabbeva pādesu nipatitvā sirasā vandiṃsu. Atha ne ācariyo āha – “tātā, amhākaṃ buddhānaṃ anucchaviko deyyadhammo natthi, satthā ca bhikkhācāravelāyaṃ idhāgato, mayaṃ yathāsatti yathābalaṃ deyyadhammaṃ dassāma, tumhe yaṃ yaṃ paṇītaṃ phalāphalaṃ, taṃ taṃ āharathā”ti āharāpetvā hatthe dhovitvā sayaṃ tathāgatassa patte patiṭṭhāpesi. Satthārā phalāphale paṭiggahitamatte devatā dibbojaṃ pakkhipiṃsu. So tāpaso udakampi sayameva parissāvetvā adāsi. Tato bhattakiccaṃ katvā nisinne satthari sabbe antevāsike pakkositvā satthu santike sāraṇīyakathaṃ kathento nisīdi. Satthā “dve aggasāvakā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ āgacchantū”ti cintesi. Te satthu cittaṃ ñatvā satasahassakhīṇāsavaparivārā āgantvā satthāraṃ vanditvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhaṃsu.

At that time, seventy-four thousand matted-hair ascetics, taking excellent and nourishing large and small fruits, approached their teacher. Observing the seat where the Buddha and their teacher were seated, they said, 'Teacher, we have considered that in this world there is no one greater than you, but this man, it seems, is greater than you.' 'Dear sons, what are you saying? Do you wish to make Mount Sineru, which is one million, sixty-eight thousand yojanas high, equal with a mustard seed? My dear sons, do not make a comparison of me with the Omniscient Buddha.' Then those ascetics thought, 'If this were a mere being, our teacher would not have brought forth such a comparison. How great, indeed, is this man!' And they all, falling at his feet, paid homage with their heads. Then their teacher said to them, 'Dear sons, we have no gift suitable for the Buddhas. And the Teacher has come here at the time for the alms-round. We shall give a gift according to our ability and according to our strength. You all, bring whatever excellent large and small fruits there are.' Having had them brought, he washed his hands and himself placed them in the Tathāgata’s bowl. Just as the Teacher accepted the large and small fruits, the deities infused them with divine nutriment. That ascetic, having strained the water himself, also gave it. Then, after the Teacher had finished his meal and was seated, the ascetic, having summoned all his disciples, sat in the Teacher's presence, engaging in memorable and courteous conversation. The Teacher thought, 'Let the two chief disciples come with the community of bhikkhus.' They, knowing the Teacher's thought, arrived with a retinue of one hundred thousand who had destroyed the taints, paid homage to the Teacher, and stood to one side.

Tato [M 1.0069] saradatāpaso [P 1.0108] antevāsike āmantesi – “tātā, buddhānaṃ nisinnāsanampi nīcaṃ, samaṇasatasahassānampi āsanaṃ natthi, ajja tumhehi uḷāraṃ buddhasakkāraṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭati, pabbatapādato vaṇṇagandhasampannāni pupphāni āharathā”ti. Kathanakālo papañco viya hoti, iddhimato [V 1.0063] pana iddhivisayo acinteyyoti muhuttamatteneva te tāpasā vaṇṇagandhasampannāni pupphāni āharitvā buddhānaṃ yojanappamāṇaṃ pupphāsanaṃ paññāpesuṃ. Ubhinnaṃ aggasāvakānaṃ tigāvutaṃ, sesabhikkhūnaṃ aḍḍhayojanikādibhedaṃ, saṅghanavakassa usabhamattaṃ ahosi. “Kathaṃ ekasmiṃ assamapade tāva mahantāni āsanāni paññattānī”ti na cintetabbaṃ. Iddhivisayo hesa. Evaṃ paññattesu āsanesu saradatāpaso tathāgatassa purato añjaliṃ paggayha ṭhito, “bhante, mayhaṃ dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāya imaṃ pupphāsanaṃ abhiruhathā”ti āha. Tena vuttaṃ –

Then the ascetic Sarada addressed his disciples: 'Dear sons, the Buddha's seat is low, and for the one hundred thousand monks, there are no seats. Today it is fitting for you to perform a magnificent honor to the Buddha. Bring flowers endowed with color and fragrance from the foot of the mountain.' The time of speaking seems prolonged, but the sphere of power of one with psychic power is inconceivable. Therefore, in just a moment, those ascetics brought flowers endowed with color and fragrance and prepared a flower-seat of one yojana in measure for the Buddha. For the two chief disciples, it was three gāvutas; for the remaining bhikkhus, it was of various sizes such as half a yojana; and for the most junior in the Sangha, it was the measure of one usabha. One should not think, 'How in one hermitage were such great seats prepared?' Indeed, this is the sphere of psychic power. When the seats were thus prepared, the ascetic Sarada, standing before the Tathāgata with his hands raised in añjali, said, 'Venerable Sir, for my welfare and happiness for a long time, please ascend this flower-seat.' Therefore, it was said:

“Nānāpupphañca gandhañca, sampādetvāna ekato;

Pupphāsanaṃ paññāpetvā, idaṃ vacanamabravi.

Having procured various flowers and fragrances together, and having prepared a seat of flowers, he spoke these words:

“Idaṃ me āsanaṃ vīra, paññattaṃ tavanucchaviṃ;

Mama cittaṃ pasādento, nisīda pupphamāsane.

O Hero, this seat, suitable for you, has been prepared by me. Inspiring serenity in my mind, please be seated on this flower-seat.

“Sattarattindivaṃ buddho, nisīdi pupphamāsane;

Mama cittaṃ pasādetvā, hāsayitvā sadevake”ti.

The Buddha, for seven nights and days, sat upon the flower-seat, making my mind serene and causing the world with its devas to rejoice.

Evaṃ nisinne satthari dve aggasāvakā sesabhikkhū ca [P 1.0109] attano attano pattāsane nisīdiṃsu. Saradatāpaso mahantaṃ pupphacchattaṃ gahetvā tathāgatassa matthake dhārento aṭṭhāsi. Satthā “jaṭilānaṃ ayaṃ sakkāro mahapphalo hotū”ti nirodhasamāpattiṃ samāpajji. Satthu samāpattiṃ samāpannabhāvaṃ ñatvā dve aggasāvakāpi sesabhikkhūpi samāpattiṃ samāpajjiṃsu. Tathāgate sattāhaṃ nirodhasamāpattiṃ samāpajjitvā nisinne antevāsikā bhikkhācārakāle sampatte vanamūlaphalāphalaṃ paribhuñjitvā sesakāle buddhānaṃ añjaliṃ paggayha tiṭṭhanti. Saradatāpaso pana bhikkhācārampi agantvā pupphacchattaṃ dhārayamānova sattāhaṃ pītisukhena vītināmesi. Satthā nirodhato vuṭṭhāya dakkhiṇapasse nisinnaṃ paṭhamaaggasāvakaṃ nisabhattheraṃ āmantesi – “nisabha, sakkārakārakānaṃ [M 1.0070] tāpasānaṃ pupphāsanānumodanaṃ karohī”ti. Thero cakkavattirañño santikā paṭiladdhamahālābho mahāyodho viya tuṭṭhamānaso sāvakapāramiñāṇe ṭhatvā pupphāsanānumodanaṃ ārabhi. Tassa desanāvasāne dutiyasāvakaṃ āmantesi – “tvampi bhikkhu dhammaṃ desehī”ti. Anomatthero tepiṭakaṃ buddhavacanaṃ sammasitvā dhammaṃ kathesi. Dvinnaṃ aggasāvakānaṃ desanāya ekassāpi abhisamayo nāhosi. Atha satthā aparimāṇe buddhavisaye ṭhatvā dhammadesanaṃ ārabhi. Desanāpariyosāne ṭhapetvā saradatāpasaṃ sabbepi catusattatisahassajaṭilā arahattaṃ pāpuṇiṃsu[V 1.0064], satthā “etha, bhikkhavo”ti hatthaṃ pasāresi. Tesaṃ tāvadeva kesamassūni antaradhāyiṃsu, aṭṭhaparikkhārā kāye paṭimukkāva ahesuṃ.

When the Teacher was thus seated, the two chief disciples and the remaining bhikkhus sat on their respective allotted seats. The ascetic Sarada, taking a large flower-parasol, stood holding it over the Tathāgata's head. The Teacher, thinking, 'May this honor from the matted-hair ascetics be of great fruit,' entered the attainment of cessation. Knowing that the Teacher had entered the attainment, the two chief disciples and the remaining bhikkhus also entered the attainment. While the Tathāgata was seated for seven days, having entered the attainment of cessation, the disciples, when the time for the alms-round arrived, consumed forest roots and fruits; during the remaining time, they stood with hands raised in añjali towards the Buddhas. The ascetic Sarada, however, not even going for the alms-round, spent seven days with the happiness of rapture while continuing to hold the flower-parasol. The Teacher, having emerged from cessation, addressed the Elder Nisabha, the first chief disciple, seated on his right side: 'Nisabha, give the rejoicing for the flower-seat to the ascetics who made the offering.' The Elder, with a delighted mind like a great general who has received a great reward from a universal monarch, standing firm in the knowledge of a disciple's perfection, began the rejoicing for the flower-seat. At the end of his discourse, the Teacher addressed the second disciple: 'You too, bhikkhu, teach the Dhamma.' The Elder Anoma, having reflected upon the Tipiṭaka, the word of the Buddha, taught the Dhamma. Through the discourses of both chief disciples, not even one person had a penetration of the Dhamma. Then the Teacher, standing in the immeasurable sphere of a Buddha, began the discourse on the Dhamma. At the end of the discourse, excepting the ascetic Sarada, all seventy-four thousand matted-hair ascetics attained Arahantship. The Teacher extended his hand, saying, 'Come, bhikkhus.' At that very moment, their hair and beards vanished, and the eight requisites were upon their bodies as if already put on.

Saradatāpaso “kasmā arahattaṃ na patto”ti? Vikkhittacittattā. So kira buddhānaṃ dutiyāsane [P 1.0110] nisīditvā sāvakapāramiñāṇe ṭhatvā dhammaṃ desayato aggasāvakassa dhammadesanaṃ sotuṃ āraddhakālato paṭṭhāya, “aho vatāhampi anāgate uppajjanakabuddhassa sāsane iminā sāvakena paṭiladdhadhuraṃ labheyya”nti cittaṃ uppādesi. So tena parivitakkena maggaphalapaṭivedhaṃ kātuṃ nāsakkhi. Tathāgataṃ pana vanditvā sammukhe ṭhatvā āha – “bhante, tumhākaṃ anantarāsane nisinno bhikkhu tumhākaṃ sāsane ko nāma hotī”ti? “Mayā pavattitaṃ dhammacakkaṃ anupavattento sāvakapāramiñāṇassa koṭippatto soḷasa paññā paṭivijjhitvā ṭhito mayhaṃ sāsane aggasāvako nisabho nāma eso”ti. “Bhante, yvāyaṃ mayā sattāhaṃ pupphacchattaṃ dhārentena sakkāro kato, ahaṃ imassa phalena aññaṃ sakkattaṃ vā brahmattaṃ vā na patthemi, anāgate pana ayaṃ nisabhatthero viya ekassa buddhassa aggasāvako bhaveyya”nti patthanaṃ akāsinti. Satthā “samajjhissati nu kho imassa purisassa patthanā”ti anāgataṃsañāṇaṃ pesetvā olokento kappasatasahassādhikaṃ ekaṃ asaṅkhyeyyaṃ atikkamitvā samijjhanabhāvaṃ addasa. Disvāna saradatāpasaṃ āha – “na te ayaṃ patthanā moghā bhavissati, anāgate pana kappasatasahassādhikaṃ ekaṃ asaṅkhyeyyaṃ atikkamitvā gotamo nāma buddho uppajjissati, tassa mātā mahāmāyā [M 1.0071] nāma devī bhavissati, pitā suddhodano nāma mahārājā, putto rāhulo nāma, upaṭṭhāko ānando nāma, dutiyaaggasāvako moggallāno nāma, tvaṃ panassa paṭhamaaggasāvako dhammasenāpati sāriputto nāma bhavissasī”ti[P 1.0111]. Evaṃ tāpasaṃ byākaritvā dhammakathaṃ kathetvā bhikkhusaṅghaparivuto ākāsaṃ pakkhandi.

Why did the ascetic Sarada not attain Arahantship? Because his mind was distracted. It is said that from the time he began to listen to the Dhamma discourse of the chief disciple, who was seated in the second seat of the Buddhas, established in the knowledge of a disciple's perfections, and was teaching the Dhamma, he gave rise to this thought: 'Oh, may I too, in the future, in the Dispensation of a Buddha who will arise, obtain the foremost position that has been obtained by this disciple!' Due to that reflection, he was unable to penetrate the path and its fruit. Then, having paid homage to the Tathāgata and standing in his presence, he asked, 'Venerable Sir, the monk seated in the seat next to you, what is his name in your Dispensation?' 'He who turns the Wheel of Dhamma after I have set it in motion, who has reached the pinnacle of the knowledge of a disciple's perfections by penetrating it with the sixteen knowledges, and stands firm—this one is my chief disciple in my Dispensation, named Nisabha.' 'Venerable Sir, for the homage I have paid by holding a floral parasol for seven days, I do not, with its fruit, aspire for any other state, such as that of a Sakka or a Brahmā. But in the future, may I become the chief disciple of a certain Buddha, just like this Elder Nisabha.' Thus he made his aspiration. The Teacher, thinking, 'Will this man's aspiration be fulfilled?', sent forth his knowledge of the future and, looking, saw that it would be fulfilled after passing beyond one incalculable aeon and a hundred thousand kappas. Having seen this, he said to the ascetic Sarada: 'This aspiration of yours will not be in vain. In the future, after passing beyond one incalculable aeon and a hundred thousand kappas, a Buddha named Gotama will arise. His mother will be Queen Mahāmāyā, his father King Suddhodana, his son Rāhula, his attendant Ānanda, and his second chief disciple Moggallāna. You, however, will be his first chief disciple, the General of the Dhamma, named Sāriputta.' Having thus given the prediction to the ascetic and delivered a Dhamma discourse, surrounded by the community of monks, he ascended into the sky.

Saradatāpasopi antevāsikattherānaṃ santikaṃ gantvā sahāyakassa sirivaḍḍhanakuṭumbikassa sāsanaṃ pesesi, “bhante, mama sahāyakassa vadetha, sahāyakena te saradatāpasena anomadassībuddhassa pādamūle anāgate uppajjanakassa gotamabuddhassa sāsane paṭhamaaggasāvakaṭṭhānaṃ patthitaṃ, tvaṃ dutiyaaggasāvakaṭṭhānaṃ patthehī”ti. Evañca pana vatvā therehi puretarameva ekapassena gantvā sirivaḍḍhanassa nivesanadvāre aṭṭhāsi. Sirivaḍḍhano “cirassaṃ vata me ayyo āgato”ti āsane nisīdāpetvā attanā nīcāsane nisinno, “antevāsikaparisā pana vo, bhante, na paññāyatī”ti pucchi. “Āma, samma, amhākaṃ assamaṃ anomadassī buddho āgato, mayaṃ tassa attano balena sakkāraṃ akarimhā, satthā sabbesaṃ [V 1.0065] dhammaṃ desesi, desanāpariyosāne ṭhapetvā maṃ sesā arahattaṃ patvā pabbajiṃsu. Ahaṃ satthu paṭhamaaggasāvakaṃ nisabhattheraṃ disvā anāgate uppajjanakassa gotamabuddhassa nāma sāsane paṭhamaaggasāvakaṭṭhānaṃ patthesiṃ, tvampi tassa sāsane dutiyaaggasāvakaṭṭhānaṃ patthehī”ti. “Mayhaṃ buddhehi saddhiṃ paricayo natthi, bhante”ti. “Buddhehi saddhiṃ kathanaṃ mayhaṃ bhāro hotu, tvaṃ mahantaṃ sakkāraṃ sajjehī”ti.

The ascetic Sarada also, having gone to his resident elder disciples, sent a message to his friend, the householder Sirivaḍḍhana, saying: 'Venerable Sirs, please tell my friend: "Your friend, the ascetic Sarada, at the feet of the Buddha Anomadassī, has aspired to the position of first chief disciple in the Dispensation of the future Buddha Gotama. You should aspire to the position of second chief disciple."' And having said this, he went ahead of the elders by a separate path and stood at the door of Sirivaḍḍhana's residence. Sirivaḍḍhana, thinking, 'My noble master has come after a long time!', had him sit on a seat, while he himself sat on a low seat. He then asked, 'Venerable Sir, your retinue of resident disciples is not to be seen?' 'Yes, friend. The Buddha Anomadassī came to our hermitage. We paid homage to him according to our ability. The Teacher taught the Dhamma to all. At the end of the discourse, all the others, except for me, attained Arahantship and went forth. Having seen the Teacher's first chief disciple, the Elder Nisabha, I aspired to the position of first chief disciple in the Dispensation of the future Buddha named Gotama. You too should aspire to the position of second chief disciple in his Dispensation.' 'Venerable Sir, I have no acquaintance with Buddhas.' 'Let speaking with the Buddhas be my responsibility. You prepare a great offering.'

Sirivaḍḍhano tassa vacanaṃ sutvā attano nivesanadvāre rājamānena aṭṭhakarīsamattaṃ ṭhānaṃ samatalaṃ kāretvā vālukaṃ okirāpetvā [P 1.0112] lājapañcamānipupphāni vikirāpetvā nīluppalacchadanaṃ maṇḍapaṃ kāretvā buddhāsanaṃ paññāpetvā sesabhikkhūnampi āsanāni paṭiyādetvā mahantaṃ sakkārasammānaṃ sajjetvā buddhānaṃ nimantanatthāya saradatāpasassa saññaṃ adāsi. Tāpaso buddhappamukhaṃ bhikkhusaṅghaṃ gahetvā tassa nivesanaṃ agamāsi. Sirivaḍḍhanopi paccuggamanaṃ katvā tathāgatassa hatthato pattaṃ gahetvā maṇḍapaṃ pavesetvā paññattāsanesu nisinnassa buddhappamukhassa bhikkhusaṅghassa dakkhiṇodakaṃ [M 1.0072] datvā paṇītena bhojanena parivisitvā bhattakiccapariyosāne buddhappamukhaṃ bhikkhusaṅghaṃ mahārahehi vatthehi acchādetvā, “bhante, nāyaṃ ārabbho appamattakaṭṭhānatthāya, imināva niyāmena sattāhaṃ anukampaṃ karothā”ti āha. Satthā adhivāsesi. So teneva niyāmena sattāhaṃ mahādānaṃ pavattetvā bhagavantaṃ vanditvā añjaliṃ paggayha ṭhito āha – “bhante, mama sahāyo saradatāpaso yassa satthussa paṭhamaaggasāvako bhaveyya”nti patthesi, ahampi “tasseva dutiyaaggasāvako bhaveyya”nti patthemīti.

Sirivaḍḍhana, having heard his words, had a space of about eight karīsas by the royal measure leveled near the door of his residence, had sand scattered, had flowers with parched rice as the fifth kind scattered about, and had a pavilion roofed with blue water lilies constructed. He had the Buddha's seat prepared, had seats prepared for the remaining monks as well, and having arranged great veneration and honor, he gave a signal to the ascetic Sarada to invite the Buddha. The ascetic, taking the community of monks with the Buddha at its head, went to his residence. Sirivaḍḍhana also went out to meet them, took the bowl from the Tathāgata's hand, led them into the pavilion, and having poured the water of dedication for the community of monks headed by the Buddha who were seated on the prepared seats, he served them with exquisite food. At the conclusion of the meal, he covered the community of monks headed by the Buddha with costly cloths and said, 'Venerable Sir, this endeavor is not for a trifling purpose; please show your compassion in this same way for seven days.' The Teacher consented. For seven days, he continued the great offering in that same manner. Then, having paid homage to the Blessed One and standing with his hands raised in reverence, he said: 'Venerable Sir, my friend, the ascetic Sarada, made the aspiration, "May I be the first chief disciple of whichever Teacher there might be." I too make the aspiration, "May I be the second chief disciple of that very same Teacher."

Satthā anāgataṃ oloketvā tassa patthanāya samijjhanabhāvaṃ disvā byākāsi – “tvaṃ ito kappasatasahassādhikaṃ asaṅkhyeyyaṃ atikkamitvā gotamabuddhassa dutiyaaggasāvako bhavissasī”ti. Buddhānaṃ byākaraṇaṃ sutvā sirivaḍḍhano haṭṭhapahaṭṭho ahosi. Satthāpi bhattānumodanaṃ katvā saparivāro vihārameva gato. “Ayaṃ, bhikkhave, mama puttehi tadā patthitapatthanā. Te yathāpatthitameva labhiṃsu. Nāhaṃ mukhaṃ oloketvā demī”ti.

The Teacher, looking into the future and seeing that his aspiration would be fulfilled, made a prediction: 'You, after passing beyond one incalculable aeon and an additional one hundred thousand world-cycles from now, will become the second chief disciple of the Buddha Gotama.' Hearing the Buddha's prediction, Sirivaḍḍhana was extremely joyful. The Teacher, too, after giving the discourse of rejoicing for the meal, went back to the monastery with his retinue. 'Monks, this was the aspiration made by my sons at that time. They obtained exactly what they had aspired for. I do not give by looking at faces.'

Evaṃ [P 1.0113] vutte dve aggasāvakā bhagavantaṃ vanditvā, “bhante, mayaṃ agāriyabhūtā samānā giraggasamajjaṃ dassanāya gatā”ti yāva assajittherassa santikā sotāpattiphalapaṭivedhā sabbaṃ paccuppannavatthuṃ kathetvā, “te mayaṃ, bhante, ācariyassa sañcayassa santikaṃ gantvā taṃ tumhākaṃ pādamūle ānetukāmā tassa laddhiyā nissārabhāvaṃ kathetvā idhāgamane ānisaṃsaṃ kathayimhā. So idāni mayhaṃ antevāsikavāso nāma cāṭiyā udañcanabhāvappattisadiso, na sakkhissāmi [V 1.0066] antevāsivāsaṃ vasitu”nti vatvā, “ācariya, idāni mahājano gandhamālādihattho gantvā satthārameva pūjessati, tumhe kathaṃ bhavissathā”ti vutte “kiṃ pana imasmiṃ loke paṇḍitā bahū, udāhu dandhā”ti? “Dandhā”ti kathite “tena hi paṇḍitā paṇḍitassa samaṇassa gotamassa santikaṃ gamissanti, dandhā dandhassa mama santikaṃ āgamissanti, gacchatha tumhe”ti vatvā “āgantuṃ na icchi, bhante”ti. Taṃ sutvā satthā, “bhikkhave, sañcayo attano micchādiṭṭhitāya asāraṃ sāroti, sārañca asāroti gaṇhi. Tumhe pana attano paṇḍitatāya sārañca sārato, asārañca asārato ñatvā asāraṃ pahāya sārameva gaṇhitthā”ti vatvā imā gāthā abhāsi –

When this was said, the two chief disciples, having paid homage to the Blessed One, said: 'Venerable Sir, while we were householders, we went to see the festival on the mountain-top.' They then related the entire present story, up to their penetration of the fruit of stream-entry in the presence of the Elder Assaji, and continued: 'Then, Venerable Sir, desiring to bring our teacher Sañjaya to your feet, we went to his presence. We spoke of the essenceless nature of his doctrine and explained the benefits of coming here. He, however, said: "For me to now live as a disciple would be like a large water pot becoming a small water ladle. I will not be able to live the life of a disciple." When we said, "Teacher, the great populace will now go with perfumes, garlands, and so on in hand to worship only the Teacher; what will become of you?" he asked, "In this world, are the wise many, or are the slow-witted many?" When it was said, "The slow-witted are many," he replied, "In that case, the wise will go to the presence of the wise ascetic Gotama, and the slow-witted will come to me, the slow-witted one. You may go." Thus, Venerable Sir, he did not wish to come.' Hearing this, the Teacher said: 'Monks, Sañjaya, due to his own wrong view, grasps the essenceless as essence and the essence as essenceless. But you, through your wisdom, having known the essence as essence and the essenceless as essenceless, should abandon the essenceless and grasp only the essence.' Having said this, he spoke these verses:

11.

11.

“Asāre [M 1.0073] sāramatino, sāre cāsāradassino;

Te sāraṃ nādhigacchanti, micchāsaṅkappagocarā.

Those who consider the unessential to be essential, and see the essential as unessential, do not attain the essence, for they range in the sphere of wrong intention.

12.

12.

“Sārañca [P 1.0114] sārato ñatvā, asārañca asārato;

Te sāraṃ adhigacchanti, sammāsaṅkappagocarā”ti.

Those who have known the essential as essential, and the unessential as unessential, attain the essence, for they range in the sphere of right intention.

Tattha asāre sāramatinoti cattāro paccayā, dasavatthukā micchādiṭṭhi, tassā upanissayabhūtā dhammadesanāti ayaṃ asāro nāma, tasmiṃ sāradiṭṭhinoti attho. Sāre cāsāradassinoti dasavatthukā sammādiṭṭhi, tassā upanissayabhūtā dhammadesanāti ayaṃ sāro nāma, tasmiṃ “nāyaṃ sāro”ti asāradassino. Te sāranti te pana taṃ micchādiṭṭhiggahaṇaṃ gahetvā ṭhitā kāmavitakkādīnaṃ vasena micchāsaṅkappagocarā hutvā sīlasāraṃ, samādhisāraṃ, paññāsāraṃ, vimuttisāraṃ, vimuttiñāṇadassanasāraṃ, “paramatthasāraṃ, nibbānañca nādhigaccha”nti. Sārañcāti tameva sīlasārādisāraṃ “sāro nāmāya”nti, vuttappakārañca asāraṃ “asāro aya”nti ñatvā. Te sāranti te paṇḍitā evaṃ sammādassanaṃ gahetvā ṭhitā nekkhammasaṅkappādīnaṃ vasena sammāsaṅkappagocarā hutvā taṃ vuttappakāraṃ sāraṃ adhigacchantīti.

Herein, regarding 'regarding the unessential as essential': the unessential is the four requisites, the ten-fold wrong view, and the Dhamma teaching that is its supporting condition. To have the view of 'essence' in that, is the meaning. Regarding 'and seeing the essential as unessential': the essential is the ten-fold right view, and the Dhamma teaching that is its supporting condition. To see that as 'this is not the essence' is to be one who sees the essential as unessential. Regarding 'they do not attain the essence': those persons, having taken up and abided in that grasp of wrong view, having a sphere of wrong intention by way of sensual thoughts and so on, do not attain the essence of virtue, the essence of concentration, the essence of wisdom, the essence of liberation, the essence of the knowledge and vision of liberation, the ultimate essence, and Nibbāna. Regarding 'knowing the essential as essential': it means knowing that very essence of virtue and so on as 'this is essence', and the aforementioned unessential as 'this is unessential'. Regarding 'they attain the essence': those wise ones, having thus taken up and abided in right view, having a sphere of right intention by way of thoughts of renunciation and so on, attain that aforesaid essence.

Gāthāpariyosāne bahū sotāpattiphalādīni pāpuṇiṃsu. Sannipatitānaṃ sātthikā dhammadesanā ahosīti.

At the conclusion of the verses, many attained the fruit of stream-entry and so on. For the assembled congregation, the Dhamma teaching was beneficial.

Sāriputtattheravatthu aṭṭhamaṃ.

The Eighth Story of the Elder Sāriputta.

9. Nandattheravatthu

9. The Story of the Elder Nanda

Yathā [V 1.0067][P 1.0115] agāranti imaṃ dhammadesanaṃ satthā jetavane viharanto āyasmantaṃ nandaṃ ārabbha kathesi.

The Teacher, while dwelling at Jetavana, delivered this Dhamma discourse beginning with the words, 'Yathā agāraṃ,' concerning the Venerable Nanda.

Satthā hi pavattitavaradhammacakko rājagahaṃ gantvā veḷuvane viharanto – “puttaṃ me ānetvā dassethā”ti suddhodanamahārājena pesitānaṃ sahassasahassaparivārānaṃ dasannaṃ dūtānaṃ sabbapacchato gantvā arahattappattena kāḷudāyittherena gamanakālaṃ ñatvā maggavaṇṇaṃ vaṇṇetvā vīsatisahassakhīṇāsavaparivuto [M 1.0074] kapilapuraṃ nīto ñātisamāgame pokkharavassaṃ atthuppattiṃ katvā vessantarajātakaṃ (jā. 2.22.1655 ādayo) kathetvā punadivase piṇḍāya paviṭṭho, “uttiṭṭhe nappamajjeyyā”ti (dha. pa. 168) gāthāya pitaraṃ sotāpattiphale patiṭṭhāpetvā, “dhammañcare”ti (dha. pa. 169) gāthāya mahāpajāpatiṃ sotāpattiphale, rājānañca sakadāgāmiphale patiṭṭhāpesi. Bhattakiccāvasāne pana rāhulamātuguṇakathaṃ nissāya candakinnarījātakaṃ (jā. 1.14.18 ādayo) kathetvā tato tatiyadivase nandakumārassa abhisekagehappavesanavivāhamaṅgalesu pavattamānesu piṇḍāya pavisitvā nandakumārassa hatthe pattaṃ datvā maṅgalaṃ vatvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkamanto nandakumārassa hatthato pattaṃ na gaṇhi. Sopi tathāgatagāravena “pattaṃ vo, bhante, gaṇhathā”ti vattuṃ nāsakkhi. Evaṃ pana cintesi – “sopānasīse pattaṃ gaṇhissatī”ti. Satthā tasmimpi ṭhāne na gaṇhi. Itaro “sopānapādamūle gaṇhissatī”ti cintesi. Satthā tatthāpi na [P 1.0116] gaṇhi. Itaro “rājaṅgaṇe gaṇhissatī”ti cintesi. Satthā tatthāpi na gaṇhi. Kumāro nivattitukāmo aruciyā gacchanto satthugāravena “pattaṃ gaṇhathā”ti vattuṃ na sakkoti. “Idha gaṇhissati, ettha gaṇhissatī”ti cintento gacchati.

Indeed, the Teacher, having set in motion the excellent Wheel of the Dhamma, went to Rājagaha and dwelt in the Veḷuvana Monastery. When the great king Suddhodana sent ten messengers, each with a retinue of a thousand, saying, 'Bring my son and show him to me,' the Elder Kāḷudāyī, who had attained Arahantship, went last of all. Knowing the time for the journey, he praised the path and led the Teacher, surrounded by twenty thousand who had destroyed the taints, to the city of Kapila. At the gathering of his kinsmen, having created the occasion of the pokkhara rain, he related the Vessantara Jātaka. On the next day, having entered for alms-food, he established his father in the fruit of stream-entry with the verse beginning, 'Uttiṭṭhe nappamajjeyya.' With the verse beginning, 'Dhammañcare,' he established Mahāpajāpatī in the fruit of stream-entry, and the king in the fruit of once-returning. Then, at the conclusion of the meal, based on a talk about the virtues of Rāhula's mother, he related the Candakinnarī Jātaka. From then, on the third day, while the consecration, house-warming, and wedding ceremonies of Prince Nanda were taking place, the Teacher entered for alms-food. Having placed the bowl in Prince Nanda's hand and spoken a blessing, he rose from his seat and departed, but did not take the bowl from Prince Nanda's hand. Nanda, out of reverence for the Tathāgata, was unable to say, 'Venerable Sir, take your bowl.' Instead, he thought, 'He will take the bowl at the head of the stairs.' But the Teacher did not take it even in that place. The other thought, 'He will take it at the foot of the stairs.' The Teacher did not take it there either. The other thought, 'He will take it in the royal courtyard.' The Teacher did not take it there either. The prince, though wishing to turn back, went on unwillingly. Out of reverence for the Teacher, he was unable to say, 'Take the bowl.' Thinking, 'He will take it here, he will take it there,' he went on.

Tasmiṃ khaṇe aññā itthiyo taṃ disvā janapadakalyāṇiyā ācikkhiṃsu – “ayye, bhagavā nandakumāraṃ gahetvā gato, tumhehi taṃ vinā karissatī”ti. Sā udakabindūhi paggharanteheva aḍḍhullikhitehi kesehi vegena gantvā, “tuvaṭaṃ kho, ayyaputta, āgaccheyyāsī”ti āha. Taṃ tassā vacanaṃ tassa hadaye tiriyaṃ patitvā viya ṭhitaṃ. Satthāpissa hatthato pattaṃ aggaṇhitvāva taṃ vihāraṃ netvā, “pabbajissasi nandā”tiāha. So buddhagāravena “na pabbajissāmī”ti avatvā, “āma, pabbajissāmī”ti āha. Satthā “tena hi nandaṃ pabbājethā”ti āha. Satthā kapilapuraṃ gantvā tatiyadivase nandaṃ pabbājesi.

At that moment, other women saw this and informed Janapadakalyāṇī, 'Madam, the Blessed One has taken Prince Nanda and gone. What will you do without him?' Hearing this, with her hair half-combed and water drops dripping from it, she went quickly and said, 'Noble prince, please come back quickly!' Those words of hers remained in his heart as if they had fallen sideways upon it. The Teacher, without taking the bowl from his hand, led him to the monastery and asked, 'Nanda, will you go forth?' Out of reverence for the Buddha, not daring to say, 'I will not go forth,' he said, 'Yes, I will go forth.' The Teacher said, 'In that case, have Nanda go forth.' The Teacher, having gone to the city of Kapila, ordained Nanda on the third day.

Sattame [V 1.0068] divase rāhulamātā kumāraṃ alaṅkaritvā bhagavato santikaṃ pesesi – “passa, tāta, etaṃ vīsatisahassasamaṇaparivutaṃ suvaṇṇavaṇṇaṃ brahmarūpivaṇṇaṃ samaṇaṃ, ayaṃ te pitā, etassa mahantā nidhikumbhiyo ahesuṃ. Tyāssa nikkhamanato paṭṭhāya na passāma, gaccha naṃ dāyajjaṃ yācassu – ‘ahaṃ[M 1.0075], tāta, kumāro, abhisekaṃ patvā cakkavattī bhavissāmi, dhanena me attho, dhanaṃ me dehi. Sāmiko hi putto pitusantakassā’”ti. Kumāro bhagavato santikaṃ gantvāva pitusinehaṃ paṭilabhitvā haṭṭhacitto “sukhā te, samaṇa, chāyā”ti vatvā aññampi [P 1.0117] bahuṃ attano anurūpaṃ vadanto aṭṭhāsi. Bhagavā katabhattakicco anumodanaṃ katvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmi. Kumāropi “dāyajjaṃ me, samaṇa, dehi, dāyajjaṃ me, samaṇa, dehī”ti bhagavantaṃ anubandhi. Bhagavāpi kumāraṃ na nivattāpesi. Parijanopi bhagavatā saddhiṃ gacchantaṃ nivattetuṃ nāsakkhi. Iti so bhagavatā saddhiṃ ārāmameva agamāsi.

On the seventh day, Rāhula’s mother adorned the prince and sent him to the presence of the Blessed One, saying: 'My dear son, look at this recluse surrounded by twenty thousand recluses, golden in color, with an appearance like that of a Brahmā. This is your father. He had great jars of treasure. Since his renunciation, we have not seen them. Go and ask for your inheritance: "Father, I am a prince. When I am consecrated, I will become a wheel-turning monarch. I have need of wealth; give me my wealth. For a son is indeed the owner of his father’s property."' The prince went to the Blessed One and, upon gaining a father's affection, said with a joyful heart, 'O recluse, your shade is pleasant!' and stood there speaking many other things suitable for himself. The Blessed One, having finished the duty of the meal and given the discourse of appreciation, rose from his seat and departed. The prince also followed the Blessed One, saying, 'Recluse, give me my inheritance! Recluse, give me my inheritance!' The Blessed One did not make the prince turn back. The retinue was also unable to make him turn back as he went with the Blessed One. Thus, he went right to the monastery with the Blessed One.

Tato bhagavā cintesi – “yaṃ ayaṃ pitusantakaṃ dhanaṃ icchati, taṃ vaṭṭānugataṃ savighātaṃ, handassa bodhitale paṭiladdhaṃ sattavidhaṃ ariyadhanaṃ demi, lokuttaradāyajjassa naṃ sāmikaṃ karomī”ti. Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ āmantesi – “tena hi tvaṃ, sāriputta, rāhulakumāraṃ pabbājehī”ti. Thero kumāraṃ pabbājesi. Pabbajite ca pana kumāre rañño adhimattaṃ dukkhaṃ uppajji. Taṃ adhivāsetuṃ asakkonto bhagavato nivedetvā, “sādhu, bhante, ayyā, mātāpitūhi ananuññātaṃ puttaṃ na pabbājeyyu”nti varaṃ yāci. Bhagavā tassa taṃ varaṃ datvā punekadivasaṃ rājanivesane katapātarāso ekamantaṃ nisinnena raññā, “bhante, tumhākaṃ dukkarakārikakāle ekā devatā maṃ upasaṅkamitvā, ‘putto te kālakato’ti āha.
